# Upcoming SaladCloud Price Changes: September 12, 2026

SaladCloud GPU and vCPU pricing is changing on September 12, 2026: 15 GPU classes drop 25% on average, while RTX 5090 and 4090 prices increase.

Jared Carpenter

Product Update SaladCloud Tue Sep 01 2026

We're updating GPU and vCPU pricing on SaladCloud to correct places where our prices had drifted out of line with demand: some classes were priced above what the market will bear, and a couple were priced below it.

These changes take effect Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 00:00 UTC, and they will impact active and running instances at that time.

## Summary Copy Anchor Link

- Prices for 15 GPU classes are coming down, by 25% on average at High Priority (individual classes fall between 16% and 38%).
- Lowest Priority pricing is staying stable, with the exception of the RTX 5080, where it comes down from $0.180 to $0.150.
- RTX 5090 and RTX 4090: we've had to raise High, Medium, and Low Priority prices on these two classes. At High Priority, the RTX 5090 moves from $0.450 to $0.500 and the RTX 4090 from $0.300 to $0.330.
- For CPU-only workloads, vCPU pricing is going up from $0.004 to $0.005 per vCPU per hour. RAM pricing is unchanged. GPU container groups aren't charged for vCPU or RAM.
- Every GPU class not listed below is unchanged.

# Earning Rate Changes: September 12

Salad earning rates change September 12, 2026: RTX 5090 and 4090 rates go up, 15 GPU classes come down at higher priority tiers, CPU payouts rise.

Jared Carpenter

Product Update SaladApp Fri Sep 04 2026

GPU prices will change on September 12th, 00:00 UTC. Before you worry, these changes include increased earnings for highly demanded GPUs, and almost all decreases are limited to specific priority tiers. See the chart below if you want to check what your future earning situation will look like. Keep reading for more context as to why we're altering our prices again.

If you're running a 5090 or a 4090, your rates are going up at High, Medium, and Low priority, since demand for those cards keeps outrunning what the network can supply. Fifteen other GPU classes are coming down, mostly at those same three tiers, while Lowest priority stays where it is on everything except the RTX 5080. CPU-only workloads are getting a raise too, covered below. And if your card isn't in the chart at all, nothing about your earnings is changing.

## Why prices are changing again Copy Anchor Link

For once, some of these changes are increases. Customer demand for the 5090 and 4090 has been outrunning what the network can supply for months now, so on September 12th those two classes get more expensive for customers, and your earning rates on them go up right along with it.

The rest of the changes are decreases across the higher priority tiers. Our lowest priority prices are already highly competitive with the market, so those aren't changing (the RTX 5080 being the one exception), but our higher tiers were overpriced, which discouraged customers from paying more for your GPUs. Needless to say, if our customers can get the same or comparable GPU resources elsewhere, at higher reliability, and cheaper than our higher priority prices, they can and will do so.

While we can't guarantee that this will lead to 100% uptime for everyone who owns the affected GPUs, we expect utilization and priority rates to both increase, leading to more Salad Balance heading into Chefs' pockets.

Payouts for CPU-only workloads are going from $0.0035 to $0.004 per hour per vCPU, which works out to a bit over 14% more for the exact same work.

results.title: SaladCloud Alternative (2026): GPU Prices vs PowerGPU
highlights:
# SaladCloud alternative: same NVIDIA GPUs, fixed prices 30% under the market

SaladCloud runs containers on thousands of consumer PCs whose owners rent out idle GPUs. That makes it the cheapest RTX 4090 and 5090 by the hour, at the cost of node churn, no SSH, no persistent disks and residential-grade networking. Payment is by card; pricing is announced to change on 12 September 2026.

 4 min read Updated 2026-10-19 PowerGPU prices live from the sheet

...

| | SaladCloud | PowerGPU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Billing | Usage-based per node-hour | Per second, no minimum, price locked at deploy |
| Payment | Card | Crypto only — USDT (TRC-20/ERC-20), BTC, XMR, LTC, ETH, TRX, SOL |
| Identity | Card | Email + password. No KYC, no card, no stored IP addresses |
| Free credit | None | None — every hour is ≥30% under the market median instead |
| Cheaper tier | Priority tiers (batch vs high) | Interruptible flat −50% (no auction) · reserved −35% (3+ months) |
| Regions | Distributed residential nodes worldwide | 32 regions on 5 continents, verified datacenters only |
| Minimums | None | None — 1× to 8× GPUs at the same per-GPU price |
| Storage | Ephemeral only — no persistent volumes | $0.08/GB/month NVMe, volumes survive instances |
| Egress | Included | $0.01/GB in and out, every region |
| Access | Containers only, no SSH; API and portal | Containers or full KVM VMs, SSH, Jupyter, REST API, CLI, Python SDK |

SaladCloud column: as published on salad.com on 2026-09-03. Details change — verify before you decide.

## SaladCloud vs PowerGPU prices, GPU by GPU

Public on-demand list prices per GPU-hour on SaladCloud's pricing page (2026-09-03) against PowerGPU's fixed rates today — every PowerGPU price is the public marketplace median × 0.70, rounded down, re-checked weekly.

| GPU | SaladCloud list | PowerGPU on-demand | PowerGPU interruptible | Difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 5090 consumer node, 32 GB | $0.25 | $0.481 | $0.240 | +92% on PowerGPU |
| RTX 4090 consumer node, 24 GB | $0.16 | $0.354 | $0.177 | +121% on PowerGPU |

Configurations differ (node sizes, tiers, regions); the note beside each card says which SaladCloud price is quoted. Negative differences mean SaladCloud is cheaper on that card.

### 10. Salad — Best for consumer-GPU inference at volume

Salad is the outlier on this list. Incorporated in March 2018, it owns no datacentres at all — it rents idle consumer GPUs from gaming PCs across 191 countries, with more than 2 million nodes registered, 450,000 earning and around 60,000 active on any given day.

The hardware is exclusively consumer: RTX 5090, 5080, 4090, 4080 and 3090 Ti down to a 3060, capped around 24 GB of VRAM. There is no H100, no A100, no NVLink and no multi-node training.

What there is, is price. An RTX 4090 costs $0.204 an hour at Batch priority and an RTX 3060 costs $0.084, billed per second, with nothing charged for cold boot, allocation or image download. For high-volume small-model inference, nothing else here comes close.

results.title: Choosing a GPU Cloud Beyond the Hourly Rate | Quandelia
highlights:
## The billing unit changes the comparison

Provider documentation reviewed on September 13, 2026 describes several distinct charging models. Rates and terms can change; the linked pricing pages are the references for a purchase.

| Service | What is metered | What to include in the estimate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod Pods | Allocated GPU compute; its pricing documentation specifies per-second billing | Time the Pod is running, plus storage and any commitment terms |
| Runpod Serverless | Worker lifetime, rounded up to seconds | Initialisation, execution and idle timeout; active workers stay running |
| SaladCloud Container Engine | Running container time, with hardware and priority determining the rate | CPU and RAM are included in the selected configuration; interrupted work may need repeating |
| Modal | GPU, CPU and memory resource time | The GPU rate alone is incomplete; warm GPU capacity can also be billed |
| Replicate | Depending on the model, hardware time or an output unit | Public-model and private-deployment billing differ; inspect the specific model |

...

Salad's billing documentation excludes allocation and image-download time from charges. Billing starts when a container runs. A model download or initialisation performed by the running application can therefore have a different cost from the platform downloading the container image.

results.title: Salad free credits: None | buildaicurrent
highlights:
Salad offers no free GPU credit and no GPU trial. The pricing page puts it in its FAQ: “Is there a free trial? No. SaladCloud and the Transcription API are pay-as-you-go with no minimum commitment, so you can start with a small, low-cost test before scaling.” There is no amount, so there is no expiry, and the pages checked do not state a card requirement for signup. Checked against the official pricing and get-started pages on 2026-09-18.

...

## Salad’s actual pitch is price, not credit

The official marketing floor is GPU rates from $0.02 per hour, with “No contracts. No minimums.” on the pricing page. That is the honest framing: Salad competes on being cheap from the first dollar rather than giving you a free window. The hardware is consumer GPUs contributed by a distributed network, which is how those rates exist.
